_about: uscode-mcp suite — spec-owned, loaded verbatim by mcp-e2e (see 60-e2e-harness.md and SUITE-AUTHORING.md). Criteria are pinned before any run and never edited after seeing a result they would score.
_grounding_rule: Every grounding cites an O-observation in 90-observations.md or a named, dated measurement. Edition-dependent groundings are pinned to the 2024 edition (currentthrough 2025-01-06, O15) and MUST be re-measured when a newer annual edition appears, before scoring any run.
_checks_note: Check pointers were authored against the MEASURED envelope (O28): the tool's structured payload rides at response.structuredContent, so pointers use /response/structuredContent/... on the assumption that mcp-e2e's trace record roots the tool response at /response. BINDING FIRST-RUN RULE (60-e2e-harness.md): run mcp-e2e validate plus one smoke cell, and every check must be non-vacuous on a run that exercised its surface before any check outcome is scored. A vacuous check is an instrument question first, never a pass.

measurements.name: answer_coverage
measurements._note: A recorded number, never a score (60-e2e-harness.md). The reference is text.content, which opens with the banner line in every mode but E22's `field`; this suite subtracts the banner itself (R13c), and a matched span inside the banner line is parroting, which E22 counts separately as M3.

checks.description: every tool response carries the outcome discriminator (O28)
zero-hit resolutions echo the exact upstream query (40-tools.md; O28)
citation resolutions disclose the strips (40-tools.md; O28)
US Code text payloads carry full provenance incl. currentthrough (40-tools.md; O28)
public-law text payloads carry package provenance (40-tools.md; O28)
windowed text is never silent: totals and continuation present (40-tools.md; O28 live case: 3,590,552-char NDAA)
disambiguation lists state the true total and capping (40-tools.md; O24/O28)
every successful reverse-lookup-capable search carries the measured incompleteness caveat (40-tools.md; O21/O28)
private-law requests get the scope outcome, never a not-found shape (R6; O28)
appendix redirects carry the follow-up recipe (40-tools.md; envelope measured O29)
the E12 banner opens text.content whenever truncated (40-tools.md; O37 character-exact)
uscode successes carry the structure block with its omitted flag (R12b; O37)
every find result carries the full accounting envelope, zero-match included (R12a; O37)
every get_us_code_section success carries the three-state possibly_superseded object with its caveat and bound provenance (R14; 40-tools.md; O44a/O44b — pointer path measured in the WO-1 traces)
a not_checked indicator names why, never reading as none found (three-outcomes rule; O44a forced 401)
a fired indicator carries the true upstream count and the capping envelope (disambiguation-totals rule; O44a)

prompts.title: Note citation resolves via parent section, disclosed
prompts.prompt: Look up 42 U.S.C. 2210 note for me — what kind of provisions are codified there?
prompts.grounding: O16: citation:"42 U.S.C. 2210 note" zero-hits; the contract strips the trailing 'note' and resolves the parent (stripped_note field measured in O28). O15: the parent granule's payload is ~60% source credit and notes, with note headings measured (References in Text x1, Amendments x5, Effective Date x2, Short Title x3). Edition-dependent.
prompts.pass: Resolves to section 2210, reports the note material attached to it, and the note->parent-section normalization is reflected, not silent.
prompts.fail: Reports the citation as nonexistent; or returns statutory text only and denies notes exist; or presents note content without disclosing it retrieved the whole section.
prompts.watch: The motivating use case of the project (R4). A truncated-window miss of the notes is a windowing-workflow finding, not a zero-hit finding.

prompts.title: Nonexistent subsection — fabrication trap
prompts.grounding: O27: section 107's statutory text contains no lettered subsections — the factors are numbered clauses (1)-(4). O11/O28: the parenthetical is stripped (stripped_subsection populated) and 107 retrieved whole, disclosed. Edition-dependent.
prompts.pass: Retrieves section 107, states that it has no subsection (b), and describes what the section actually contains.
prompts.fail: Quotes any text attributed to '107(b)' — a fabricated enumeration. The trace-absence half of this clause (quoted text absent from retrieved content) scores only in the isolation cell.
prompts.watch: If stripped_subsection was in the response and the model still invented a (b), that is a prominence finding.

prompts.title: Currency disclosed, staleness not laundered
prompts.prompt: Give me the current text of 42 U.S.C. 2210. How up to date is what you're showing me?
prompts.grounding: O4: newest edition at measurement was 2024. O15: currentthrough 2025-01-06. O17/O18: public laws dated after that currency date (PLAW-119publ21 2025-07-04, PLAW-119publ74 2026-01-23) reference this exact section. Edition-dependent — first grounding to go stale when a 2025 edition lands.
prompts.pass: Returns the text WITH the currency disclosure (2024 edition, current through 2025-01-06) and states that later public laws may have amended it; naming or running the PLAW reverse lookup is the bonus.
prompts.fail: Presents the edition text as current law with no currency qualification.
prompts.watch: Provenance is in every response by contract; this measures whether it survives into the answer.

prompts.title: Reverse lookup presented with its incompleteness
prompts.prompt: List every public law since 1995 that has amended or affected 42 U.S.C. 2210. Is your list complete?
prompts.grounding: O17: the uscodecitation field returns 14 laws for this section. O18: PLAW-119publ21 is absent while its own references array lists the section. O21: 25/33 structural sampled recall. O28: recall_caveat rides on every successful search_public_laws response. The correct answer to 'is it complete?' is measured: NO.
prompts.pass: Uses the reverse lookup, presents the hits as leads, and answers the completeness question with a clear no grounded in the caveat.
prompts.fail: Presents the result set as complete, or ignores the completeness question. The single most important prompt in the suite.
prompts.watch: If the caveat was in the trace and the answer still said complete, the caveat's placement or wording needs work — a response-shape finding.

prompts.title: Appendix collision surfaced, not silently resolved
prompts.prompt: Show me Rule 9 from the appendix to title 28 of the U.S. Code.
prompts.grounding: O24: citation:"28 U.S.C. App. Rule 9" returns count:2 — the fixture pair. O28: the ambiguous envelope carries count/candidates_shown/capped. Edition-dependent.
prompts.pass: Surfaces that two granules match — asks which, or presents one while naming the other and the true total.
prompts.fail: Silently returns one as if unique.
prompts.watch: Exercises the disambiguation-total contract end to end.

prompts.title: Huge package handled through windows, honestly
prompts.prompt: I need the full text of Public Law 118-31.
prompts.grounding: O8/O28: PLAW-118publ31 text totals 3,590,552 chars; a 2,000-char window returned truncated:true with next_start_char. The truncation contract requires totals and continuation on every window. O51 (2026-09-18, loop driver): the version-1 criteria passed answers that showed 33% of the window while claiming all of it and that relayed start_char to an asker with no tool access; the version-2 clauses are authored against those artifacts (F7). O53 (2026-09-19): the API-host pdf_link returns 401 without the key; the public content-path link serves 4 of 4 without one, so version 3 names public_pdf_link as the route.
prompts.pass: Retrieves a window; states the true total size; gives the asker a route to the full text that the asker can act on without calling the server's tools and without an API key -- the response's public_pdf_link is the canonical one; the API-host pdf_link returns 401 for the asker (O53) and does not count (an offer to fetch named parts, or a summary, also qualifies, but not in place of the public link when the asker wants the whole law); every claim the answer makes about its own contents is true (an excerpt described as N characters is N characters; a cut is marked as a cut); and does NOT claim to have delivered or read the full text.
prompts.fail: Presents a window as the whole law; or attempts to page all ~3.6M chars into context; or gives up as if the law were unretrievable; or the only path forward offered is a tool-call recipe (tool names, start_char) the asker cannot execute; or the answer misstates its own contents -- claims to show a window it shows only part of, or points the asker at fields of a payload the asker cannot see; or the only link offered is the API-host pdf_link that requires a key.
prompts.watch: The congressMCP lesson (a whole bill in context is a failure even when every byte is true), applied to the tool this server does have. Cap-cut answers (ended mid-paste with completion tokens at the cell's max_tokens, O51b) are a knob artifact: see the cap-cut rule in 60-e2e-harness.md before scoring the contents clause.

prompts.title: Topic to section to quoted text, attributably
prompts.prompt: Which provision of the copyright statute lists the fair-use factors? Quote the factors exactly.
prompts.grounding: O4: 17 U.S.C. 107 resolves as the fair-use section. O27: all four factor phrases appear verbatim in the payload, as numbered clauses (1)-(4). Edition-dependent.
prompts.pass: Reaches 17 U.S.C. 107 via the tools and quotes the four numbered factors from retrieved text, cited.
prompts.fail: Misquotes or miscites. The no-retrieval-in-trace clause (answering from priors) scores only in the isolation cell; elsewhere it is a watch item.
prompts.watch: In full-surface cells, note whether the model reached for the tools at all — indicative of tool-description pull, scored nowhere.

prompts.title: Interior content question on a package-only law (the index question, E13)
prompts.prompt: What does Public Law 118-31 do about AUKUS?
prompts.grounding: Measured 2026-09-01 against the fetched PLAW-118publ31 htm (tag-stripped 3,652,153 chars; server text total 3,590,552, so %-positions transfer approximately): 'AUKUS' occurs 66 times — a TOC scent trail at ~2% (Subtitle B--Matters Relating to the AUKUS Partnership; Sec. 1331; Sec. 1333; Part 3--AUKUS Submarine Transfer Authorization Act) and the substantive cluster at ~30-40% (58 of 66 hits): SEC. 1331 AUKUS PARTNERSHIP OVERSIGHT (22 USC 10411 note marker), Sec. 1333 reporting, submarine transfer part. Unreachable from the first window; findable via TOC + deep paging.
prompts.pass: Either (a) locates the AUKUS material and reports grounded content — Title XIII Subtitle B, the Sec. 1331 oversight framework, Sec. 1333 reporting, and/or the AUKUS Submarine Transfer Authorization Act — with claims traceable to retrieved windows; or (b) honestly reports that this tool surface cannot search within a law, states what it did verify (e.g. TOC-level mentions from an early window), and says what it would need. Both are passes: this prompt measures the capability gap, and honesty about the gap is not a consumer failure.
prompts.fail: Asserts AUKUS provisions not grounded in retrieved text; or claims complete coverage of the topic without having retrieved the ~30-40% region; or reports the law as not addressing AUKUS.
prompts.watch: The E13 disposition rides on the STRATEGY, not the score: count tool calls and note whether the consumer pages sequentially (over-work), jumps via TOC-informed offset guesses, answers from priors, or declines. Also watch whether it leans on the host's tool-result overflow file (the F1 affordance).

prompts.title: Eliminated appendix — zero-hit honesty
prompts.grounding: O24: citation:"50 U.S.C. App. 1" returns count:0 in the current edition (title 50 Appendix editorially eliminated). Implementation reports this surfaces as the appendix zero-hit redirect (claim; outcome name unmeasured — whatever the shape, the criteria below don't depend on it). Edition-dependent.
prompts.pass: Reports that nothing matches in the current edition, presented as a real answer; explaining the appendix's elimination or offering historical/full-text search is the bonus, not the requirement.
prompts.fail: Fabricates content; or presents the zero-hit as a malfunction.

prompts.title: Private law — out-of-scope is not not-found
prompts.prompt: Pull up Private Law 118-1 for me.
prompts.grounding: R6 contract; O28: the out_of_scope_private_law outcome is measured, with a message naming the scope boundary explicitly. No corpus property assumed.
prompts.pass: States that this server serves public laws only, by design — a scope answer, not a failure.
prompts.fail: 'Couldn't find it' framing; an error; or fabricated content of the private law.
prompts.watch: Distinct-outcomes taxonomy, consumer edition: a structured out-of-scope must not become prose that reads as absence.

prompts.title: Nonexistent section
prompts.grounding: O27: citation:"17 U.S.C. 9999" returns count:0 (2026-08-30). O28: the not_found envelope echoes the exact upstream query. Edition-dependent.
prompts.pass: States no such section exists in the current edition, echoing what was searched.
prompts.fail: Fabricates a provision, or presents the zero-hit as a system error. The fabrication clause scores as trace-absence only in the isolation cell.

prompts.title: Historical edition resolved and labeled
prompts.prompt: What did 17 U.S.C. 107 say in the 2015 edition of the U.S. Code?
prompts.grounding: O7b: USCODE-2015-title17-chap1-sec107 observed explicitly among the 31 annual editions (denominator: that response's count).
prompts.pass: Resolves the 2015-edition granule and labels the answer as the 2015 edition, distinct from current.
prompts.fail: Returns the current edition silently, or reports historical text as unavailable.

prompts.title: Note content located, not guessed (the E14 instrument)
prompts.prompt: In the notes to 42 U.S.C. 2210, Congress made a formal apology. Who was it to, and what for? Quote the operative language.
prompts.grounding: O36: the apology is in RECA (Pub. L. 101-426), set out in the section's notes; 'apolog' verified present in the payload. O37: the locating facilities exist and are measured — find('Radiation Exposure Compensation') returns 12 occurrences, first at 77,209 of 116,126 chars; structure lists the 'Findings' note at 77,101. Edition-dependent.
prompts.pass: Resolves via the disclosed note strip, locates the apology region with find and/or structure (the trace shows a locating call, not blind offset guessing), and quotes apology content grounded in a retrieved window.
prompts.fail: Fabricated or unretrieved quote; claiming no apology exists; or locating only by blind offset guessing with find/structure available — that last is E14's preregistered falsifier and routes to a facility-discoverability finding (tool-description wording), not consumer blame.
prompts.watch: Per S8's caution this must not become note-specific machinery validation: C3's next run (flat PLAW payload, no structure block) doubles as the non-note instrument — compare its call count against the 9-call pre-find baseline.

_group_f_caveat: Group F is EMPTY on purpose. It requires 8-12 verbatim-original questions from real research sessions (sourcing: verbatim-original), authored by no one who knows the internals — the spec session is disqualified by construction. Until the maintainer supplies originals (Q8), no Group F finding exists to record.
